diagnosis: Verrucous carcinoma with minimal invasive carcinoma
legend: Examination of the whole specimen showed verrucous carcinoma with a focus of conventional squamous cell carcinoma.
A large exophytic tumour with verrucous architecture blanketing the edentulous mandibular alveolar ridge and extending to the involve the vestibule and buccal mucosa.

A broad-based, well-differentiated epithelial proliferation with marked papillary parakeratosis and keratin plugging. Verrucous carcinoma invades the stroma evenly with well-defined pushing borders, extending below the level of the adjacent epithelium.
A bulbous, coalescing rete and an expanded spinous layer are present. A lichenoid immune response is often seen.
A lack of cytological atypia with normal maturation is usually seen in verrucous carcinoma. Rarely, mitoses may be present in the basal/parabasal layer, but without atypical mitotic forms.

There is a broad pushing border of infiltration below the level of the adjacent epithelium (taking the contour of the tongue into consideration). There are numerous papillary projections with parakeratotic crypting and church spire–type keratosis. Pleomorphism is absent.
